newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban union appeals for clothes for sugar workers.
newsitem.headline: Cuban union appeals for clothes for sugar workers.

text.p: Cuba's labour union appealed on Monday for donations of clothes and footwear for people working in the sugar cane harvest, in an illustration of how tough conditions are in the fields.

The union's weekly newspaper Trabajadores said that with at least one month of the harvest remaining clothing and boots distributed earlier to sugar workers were not sufficient or of good enough quality.

"They are simply of no use any more," the newspaper said. "The people are there, cutting, on top of machines and equipment, night and day, and all they are asking for is the necessary means to go on working," it said.

"Cane cutters and other people mobilised to work in the campaign, those who set out each dawn to do battle with threadbare clothes and broken boots, should have the vigorous support of their fellow workers."

The newspaper said donations last week in Las Tunas province consisted of such basic needs as "70 pairs of trousers, 425 T-shirts, 63 shirts, 26 pairs of shoes, 136 gloves, 18 files (for sharpening machetes) and 48 hats."

About half a million Cubans are involved each year in the sugar harvest, thousands of them manual cane cutters wading through man-high cane in intense heat. There has been concern in the past that some cutters are working with inadequate footwear, or with no gloves.
Sugar workers are paid in Cuban pesos but receive bonuses in the form of coupons that can be used to purchase some products such as soap and cooking oil normally sold in hard currency stores.

Cuba halted a five-year slump in sugar production last year thanks in part to technical improvements financed by foreign credits, but this consisted mostly of input for growing the cane, such as fertiliser.
No official target has been announced but authorities have said they expect a "modest" improvement in the 1996-97 harvest, which began last December, over last year's 4.45 million tonnes.
